title: First Past the Post: RCB Storm Into IPL 2026 Playoffs With Dharamsala Demolition
excerpt: Kohli's milestone-laden fifty and Venkatesh Iyer's unbeaten 73 seal a 23-run win over Punjab Kings, making the defending champions the first team to book a last-four berth
body:
At the foot of the Dhauladhar mountains in Dharamsala on Saturday, Royal Challengers Bengaluru clinched the first playoff berth of IPL 2026 with a commanding 23-run demolition of Punjab Kings—a result that simultaneously crowned the defending champions as the team to beat and pushed their opponents deeper into a tailspin of historic proportions.

## Kohli and Iyer orchestrate a masterclass

With the Himalayan air crisp and the HPCA Stadium heaving, it was vintage Virat Kohli who set the tone. The 37-year-old strode to the crease and unfurled a 58 off 37 deliveries, combining the audacious strokeplay of his prime with the poise of a man who has done this more times than anyone else in IPL history. His knock pushed him past 542 runs for the season—the ninth time he has breached 500 in an IPL campaign—and made him the first batter ever to accumulate 5,500 runs as an opener for a single franchise.

But it was Venkatesh Iyer who turned a strong total into an imposing one. The left-hander's unbeaten 73 off just 40 balls (eight fours, four sixes) was a display of clean hitting against a PBKS attack that had no answers. Iyer, who has quietly evolved into one of the IPL's most reliable middle-order enforcers since his move from KKR, shared a decisive 76-run partnership with Devdutt Padikkal before Tim David's cameo of 28 added the finishing touches to a total of 222 for 4.

## Punjab's freefall reaches new lows

What followed was a familiar, painful script for Punjab Kings. Their top order collapsed to 13 for 3 inside the powerplay—a recurring nightmare during what is now an unprecedented six-match losing streak. Rasikh Salam Dar, the young Kashmiri seamer who continues to announce himself on the biggest stage, ripped through the top order with figures of 3 for 36, while Bhuvneshwar Kumar's canny variations yielded 2 for 25.

Shashank Singh's battling 56 offered brief resistance, but the required rate had long spiralled beyond recovery. PBKS finished on 199 for 8, leaving their captain Shreyas Iyer—who was playing his landmark 100th IPL match—to reflect on a collapse that has turned a once table-topping campaign into a fight for mere survival. Having won their first seven of eight matches, Punjab have now lost six in succession, a turnaround that statistically ranks among the worst in IPL history.

## The bigger picture: who goes through?

RCB's 18 points from 13 matches all but guarantee them a top-two finish, which means a shot at Qualifier 1 and two chances to reach the final in Ahmedabad on May 31. Gujarat Titans (16 points) and Sunrisers Hyderabad (14 points) occupy second and third, while the final playoff spot remains a four-way dogfight involving Punjab Kings (13 points), Rajasthan Royals (12), Chennai Super Kings (12), and a resurgent Kolkata Knight Riders (9 points with games in hand).

For Andy Flower's RCB squad, the significance extends beyond arithmetic. This is a franchise that spent over a decade as the IPL's lovable underachievers before their cathartic 2025 title triumph. Qualification at the earliest opportunity signals that last year's success was no fluke—this is a team built to sustain excellence.

## The diaspora lens

For the millions of RCB supporters scattered across North America, the Gulf, Europe, and Australia, the playoff confirmation landed in the early hours or late evenings depending on time zone—but few were asleep. RCB commands arguably the most passionate global fanbase in franchise cricket, fuelled by Kohli's transcendent appeal. On Jio Hotstar, which holds exclusive international streaming rights for the IPL, the match registered among the highest concurrent overseas viewership figures of the season.

https://www.instagram.com/virat.kohli/

The diaspora dynamic cuts both ways in Dharamsala's case. The picturesque venue has become a pilgrimage site for NRI cricket tourists, with travel agencies in London, Toronto, and Dubai reporting sellout "IPL in the Himalayas" packages this season. The stadium's 23,000 capacity means tickets are among the hardest to get in the tournament—a boon for the local economy and a headache for fans who increasingly rely on streaming.

## What's next

RCB can afford to rotate their squad in the remaining league matches, with one eye on peaking for the playoffs. For Punjab Kings, every remaining fixture is now a final. Their next match against Lucknow Super Giants is a must-win, and even that might not be enough without favourable results elsewhere. The defending champions, meanwhile, will be quietly confident that the trophy is staying in Bengaluru.
